prompt: Edit this image. Keep the backlit house sign in the centre exactly as it is: the same brushed-aluminium elevation frame, the same oil-paint brushwork flowing from signal red through blush to lilac, the same soft halo, same position, size and proportions. Do not change the sign. Only add to the pale board-formed concrete wall around it: a masterful architectural drawing applied directly onto the concrete, sketched in fine graphite and charcoal line, of an ambitious, wildly inventive bamboo structure — sweeping arched bamboo poles bent into a gridshell pavilion with hand-lashed rope joints, cantilevered bamboo ribs and diagonal bracing that arc up and around the house sign like a cradle, with tapering bamboo culms showing their nodes. Layered with precise construction geometry: compass arcs, concentric circles centred on the sign, golden-ratio spirals, triangulation lines and faint dimension ticks, all drawn in delicate drafting style. Let a few areas of the drawing carry very soft translucent washes of blush pink and pale lilac. The drawing should feel like a celebrated architect's study sketched on the wall: elegant, airy, intricate, lighter in tone than the sign so the sign stays the hero, with plenty of breathing room near the edges. Same soft diffused daylight, same straight-on view, hyperrealistic texture of graphite on concrete. No text, no letters, no numbers, no watermark.
